statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Let m = len(paths). For L >= 0, say L is achievable when there exist integers s_0, ..., s_{m-1} such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, 0 <= s_i and s_i + L <= len(paths[i]), and for every i with 0 <= i < m and every k with 0 <= k < L, paths[i][s_i+k] = paths[0][s_0+k]. Then r is the largest achievable L.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000; paths is a list of m vectors with m = len(paths), 2 <= m <= 100000; the sum of len(paths[i]) over i = 0..m-1 is at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]), 0 <= paths[i][j] < n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < len(paths[i]), paths[i][j] != paths[i][j+1].

statement: For every n and paths satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result (some Std.I64 value); it does not overflow, panic, or access an index out of bounds.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000; paths is a list of m vectors with m = len(paths), 2 <= m <= 100000; the sum of len(paths[i]) over i = 0..m-1 is at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]), 0 <= paths[i][j] < n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < len(paths[i]), paths[i][j] != paths[i][j+1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(paths[i]) for every i with 0 <= i < len(paths). Equivalently, r <= min_{0 <= i < len(paths)} len(paths[i]).
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000; paths is a list of m vectors with m = len(paths), 2 <= m <= 100000; the sum of len(paths[i]) over i = 0..m-1 is at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]), 0 <= paths[i][j] < n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < len(paths[i]), paths[i][j] != paths[i][j+1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer L >= 0, if L is achievable for paths (i.e., with m = len(paths), there exist integers s_0, ..., s_{m-1} such that 0 <= s_i, s_i + L <= len(paths[i]) for all i with 0 <= i < m, and paths[i][s_i+k] = paths[0][s_0+k] for all i with 0 <= i < m and all k with 0 <= k < L), then r >= L.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r itself is achievable: with m = len(paths), there exist integers s_0, ..., s_{m-1} such that 0 <= s_i, s_i + r <= len(paths[i]) for every i with 0 <= i < m, and paths[i][s_i+k] = paths[0][s_0+k] for every i with 0 <= i < m and every k with 0 <= k < r. For r = 0 this is vacuous (take all s_i = 0).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no integer v such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(paths), v occurs in paths[i] (i.e., there exists j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]) and paths[i][j] = v).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if all paths are identical (i.e., for every i with 0 <= i < len(paths), len(paths[i]) = len(paths[0]), and for every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[0]), paths[i][j] = paths[0][j]), then r = len(paths[0]).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of indices i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(paths), r is at most the longest common subpath length of the two paths paths[i] and paths[j]. Here a length L is common to two paths A and B when there exist s, t with 0 <= s, s + L <= len(A), 0 <= t, t + L <= len(B), and A[s+k] = B[t+k] for all k with 0 <= k < L.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let rev(paths) be the list whose i-th path is paths[i] reversed, so rev(paths)[i][j] = paths[i][len(paths[i])-1-j] for 0 <= j < len(paths[i]). Then r is also the largest L >= 0 for which there exist integers t_0, ..., t_{m-1} (with m = len(paths)) such that 0 <= t_i and t_i + L <= len(rev(paths)[i]) for all i, and rev(paths)[i][t_i+k] = rev(paths)[0][t_0+k] for all i and all k with 0 <= k < L.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every permutation pi of the index set {0, 1, ..., m-1} with m = len(paths), the largest achievable common-subpath length for the reordered list paths[pi(0)], paths[pi(1)], ..., paths[pi(m-1)] is also r. Here achievable for a list of paths is defined by the same start-index condition as in the main specification, taking the first path in that list as the reference.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for the given n, for every integer n' with 1 <= n' <= 100000 and such that 0 <= paths[i][j] < n' for every i with 0 <= i < len(paths) and every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]), the function called with the same paths but with n' in place of n also returns r.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every bijection f from {0, 1, ..., n-1} to itself, let paths' be defined by paths'[i][j] = f(paths[i][j]) for all i with 0 <= i < len(paths) and all j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]). Then the largest achievable common-subpath length for paths' is also r.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer L with 0 <= L <= r, L is achievable for paths: with m = len(paths), there exist integers s_0, ..., s_{m-1} such that 0 <= s_i and s_i + L <= len(paths[i]) for every i with 0 <= i < m, and paths[i][s_i+k] = paths[0][s_0+k] for every i with 0 <= i < m and every k with 0 <= k < L. Thus shorter common subpaths exist whenever a common subpath of length r exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns r for paths and returns r' for paths', then r' <= r.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000; paths is a list of m vectors with m = len(paths), 2 <= m <= 100000; the sum of len(paths[i]) over i = 0..m-1 is at most 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < len(paths[i]), 0 <= paths[i][j] < n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < len(paths[i]), paths[i][j] != paths[i][j+1]; paths' is another list of vectors satisfying the same constraints with the same n and is obtained by inserting exactly one additional path into paths.
